function.name: finance_calculator_npv
function.description: Calculate the Net Present Value (NPV) for a series of cash flows discounted at a certain interest rate. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

discount_rate.description: The annual interest rate used to discount the cash flows. This is a float type value.

years.description: A list of years when the cash flow occurs. Default is empty array.

message.reasoning:
We need to calculate NPV for cash flows [-50k,10k,15k,20k,25k,30k] with discount rate 8% per year. Years default? If not specified, assume years correspond to indices starting from 0 or 1? Usually first cash flow at time 0 (initial investment). So we have CF0=-50000 at t=0, CF1=10000 at t=1,... CF5=30000 at t=5. Discount each CF_i/(1+r)^t. Compute.

Let's compute quickly:

r=0.08.

CF0: -50000/(1+0.08)^0 = -50000.

CF1: 10000/(1.08)^1 = 10000/1.08 ≈ 9259.2593.

CF2: 15000/(1.08)^2 = 15000/(1.1664) ≈ 12855. (Compute precisely: 15000 / 1.1664 = 12856.7)

CF3: 20000/(1.08)^3 = 20000/(1.259712) ≈ 15878. (20000/1.259712 = 15880.5)

CF4: 25000/(1.08)^4 = 25000/(1.360489) ≈ 18373. (25000/1.360489 = 18371.9)

CF5: 30000/(1.08)^5 = 30000/(1.469328) ≈ 20418. (30000/1.469328 = 20417.9)

Sum all: -50000 + 9259.26 + 12856.7 + 15880.5 + 18371.9 + 20417.9 = Let's sum positives: 9259.26+12856.7=22115.96; +15880.5=37996.46; +18371.9=56368.36; +20417.9=76786.26. Subtract 50000 gives 26786.26. So NPV ≈ $26,786.26.

But maybe they want using python function. We can call the function. Provide arguments: cash_flows and discount_rate. No years needed. Use function.
